thread:
marta: Quick sanity check — I'm assembling a fallback compatibility matrix for route-based fallbacks ahead of the GA rollout. Want to capture tokenizer, context-length, and tool-calling parity by variant+region+tier. Ping if you want in the review loop.

devon: @marta +1. Do we also include quota behavior? e.g., should premium routes be allowed to fallback to a cheaper variant that lacks tool-calls?

igor: yes include quota/tier rules. From infra/ML side we need columns for `tokenizer_compat`, `max_context`, `tool_call_support`, and `kv_cache_alignment` — tokenizer mismatches can silently break tool-call signatures.

sophia: Console/UX ask: surface incompatibilities as potential rollout blockers, not just warnings. If a fallback removes tool-calling for a customer tier, that should block the canary unless explicitly accepted.

marta: proposed policy: premium (SLA) routes must not fallback to a variant where `tool_call_support=false` unless customer-level opt-in. For standard tiers it's allowed but should annotate in the dashboard and send alerts.

devon: sensible. Also want an ordered fallback_priority list documented, e.g.:
```
1) same_tokenizer_variant
2) same_toolcall_capable_variant
3) reduced_context_variant
4) quantized_variant (last resort)
```

igor: minor tweak — prefer same_tokenizer even over tool-call in some edge cases because token offsets break function arg parsing. So ordering should be: `tokenizer > tool_call > context`.

router-bot: routing-config.testcluster updated: added `fallback_priority` field to policy schema. See /configs/fallbacks/testcluster-210111 for details. :white_check_mark:

ops-alerts: FYI we saw a small spike in 2101112000-2101112100 when eu-west fallbacks started going to a variant with different tokenization. Error rate + parser-mismatch errs up ~2.1%.

sophia: good catch. That supports blocking behavior for tool-call removal. UX suggestion: dashboard card that shows "Fallback Risk" per route with color states (green/amber/red) and a quick list of incompatibilities. Tooltip explains why (tokenizer mismatch, ctx too small, missing tool support).

marta: dropping a tiny sample CSV for the matrix so we have a shared format (feel free to suggest columns):
```
model_variant,region,tier,tokenizer_compat,max_context,tool_call_support,kv_cache_alignment,notes
llama-70b-8k,us-west,premium,true,8192,true,aligned,ok
llama-70b-4k,eu-west,standard,false,4096,false,misaligned,tokenizer mismatch - avoid for toolcalls
mistral-7b-q4,us-east,standard,true,2048,false,aligned,quantized variant - no toolcall
```

devon: test plan notes: unit tests for tokenizer token counts, integration harness that exercises `tool_call` endpoint with variant swap, and an e2e that asserts telemetry emits `fallback.reason` tag. Also add GA dashboard panels: fallback_count, fallback_error_rate, fallback_latency_p50/p95.

igor: I'll run a quick tokenizer parity script across our onboarded variants and post diffs. If mismatches >0.5% for function tokens we should mark that variant incompatible for tool-calls.

marta: awesome — schedule: sync Wednesday 10:00 PT to lock matrix + rollout gating. I'll add meeting and upload the living sheet. Thanks all :pray:

router-bot: meeting invite created: Fallback compatibility matrix sync — Wed 10:00 PT. Link: https://calendar.redwood.internal/meeting/210111-wed-fallback

ops-alerts: added a temporary alert: `fallback_tokenizer_mismatch_rate > 0.5%` to prod-eu alerts (silenced to warning).

sophia: I'll mock up the dashboard card and upload a screenshot to the doc before the sync.

marta: Perfect — see you Wed. If anyone wants to review the CSV format earlier, drop edits in the shared sheet. :rocket:
